title: Microsoft Purview: apply default SharePoint library labels to existing files (Worldwide)
summary: The briefing is supported by the roadmap, Microsoft's tenant notice and the documentation checked. Its opt-in default, licensing, policy limits and administrator controls are documented, and it accurately distinguishes this policy from the older library-default labeling behavior.

claims.claim: This is a Microsoft Purview Information Protection feature.
claims.quote: "title": "Microsoft Purview: Information Protection - Apply default SharePoint library labels to data at rest"

claims.claim: An auto-labeling policy applies a SharePoint document library's default sensitivity label to eligible files already stored there.
claims.quote: To extend your default library label deployment to existing files, create an auto-labeling policy that applies the default sensitivity label from each selected SharePoint document library to eligible existing files at rest.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; Why it matters; Governance controls; rationales
claims.claim: The feature is admin-opt-in and does not relabel existing files through this policy until an administrator creates and enables it.
claims.quote: The feature is opt-in and requires administrator configuration.

claims.claim: Microsoft's notice says default library labels previously applied only to new or modified files.
claims.quote: Previously, default library sensitivity labels were applied only to new or modified files.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: Users need not open or edit existing files for this labeling to occur.
claims.quote: Users are not required to open or edit files for labeling to occur.

claims.claim: This policy does not require sensitive information type conditions.
claims.quote: Content inspection conditions, such as sensitive information types or trainable classifiers, are not required for this policy.

claims.claim: This policy does not require trainable classifier conditions.
claims.quote: Content inspection conditions, such as sensitive information types or trainable classifiers, are not required for this policy.

claims.claim: The policy type does not inspect file content to choose a label.
claims.quote: This policy type doesn't inspect file content to choose a label.

claims.claim: The label applied to eligible files comes from their library's default sensitivity label setting.
claims.quote: The label comes from the SharePoint document library's default sensitivity label setting.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: The notice describes labeling as a background service process.
claims.quote: Labeling occurs as a background service process and is not immediate.

claims.quote: Labeling occurs as a background service process and is not immediate.

claims.claim: Unlabeled files receive the library's default sensitivity label.
claims.quote: Files that do not have a sensitivity label applied will receive the library's default sensitivity label.

claims.claim: A lower-priority existing label may be upgraded depending on policy settings.
claims.quote: Files that have a lower-priority sensitivity label applied may be upgraded to the library's default sensitivity label (depending on the policy setting).

Limitations

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Simulation identifies files in document libraries that have a default sensitivity label.
claims.quote: For this policy type, simulation identifies files in document libraries that have a default sensitivity label configured.

claims.claim: Learn recommends reviewing simulation to confirm expected sites, libraries, default labels and files before enabling the policy.
claims.quote: Review the simulation results before you turn on the policy to confirm that the expected SharePoint sites, document libraries, default library labels, and files are included.

claims.claim: Labels with user-defined permissions are unsuitable as library default labels.
claims.quote: Let users assign permissions when they apply the label and the checkbox In Word, PowerPoint, and Excel, prompt users to specify permissions is selected. This setting is sometimes referred to as "user-defined permissions".

claims.claim: A label whose user access expires at a value other than Never is unsuitable as a library default.
claims.quote: User access to content expires is set to a value other than Never.

claims.claim: A label using Double Key Encryption is unsuitable as a library default.
claims.quote:
some label configurations that apply encryption aren't suitable for SharePoint, and so don't support a default sensitivity label for a SharePoint document library:
... Double Key Encryption is selected.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: The notice names Compliance Administrator or SharePoint Administrator for configuring the policy so it can read the library default label.
claims.quote: The user configuring the policy must have either the Compliance Administrator or SharePoint Administrator role so the policy can read the default SharePoint library label.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Scope; Governance controls
claims.claim: Learn requires permission to read library metadata and names Compliance Administrator or an existing SharePoint or Microsoft Entra role with that access, such as SharePoint Administrator.
claims.quote: For the currently supported configuration path, use Compliance Administrator or an existing SharePoint or Microsoft Entra role with this access, such as SharePoint Administrator.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; controls[1].note; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: Turning a policy on after simulation requires Compliance Administrator or Compliance Data Administrator.
claims.quote: Turning a policy from Ready to turn on to On requires Compliance Administrator or Compliance Data Administrator.

claims.claim: Without one of the activation roles, Turn on policy is greyed out even after successful simulation.
claims.quote: Without one of these roles, the Turn on policy button appears greyed out even after a successful simulation.

claims.claim: The tenant-wide maximum is 500,000 automatically labeled SharePoint and OneDrive files per day across all auto-labeling policies.
claims.quote: The absolute maximum throughput is 500,000 automatically labeled SharePoint and OneDrive files per tenant per day, in aggregate across all auto-labeling policies.

claims.claim: The maximum is not a guaranteed daily labeling rate.
claims.quote: This ceiling isn't a guaranteed or consistently expected daily processing rate; actual throughput can be lower.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: PDFs are skipped entirely unless PDF labeling is enabled for the tenant.
claims.quote: If PDF labeling isn't enabled, PDFs are skipped entirely: PDFs aren't evaluated or sent for labeling, and no label is applied.

claims.quote: you can turn off this feature that supports a default sensitivity label for SharePoint document libraries. This is a tenant-level setting ... DisableDocumentLibraryDefaultLabeling ... True

claims.quote: Searched: SharePoint library default labels policy DisableDocumentLibraryDefaultLabeling stops existing files auto-labeling. claims.claim: Automatic labeling replaces a lower-priority automatically applied sensitivity label.

claims.claim: Replacing a lower-priority manually applied label is off by default.

claims.quote: The configurable setting for auto-labeling policies is on the Additional label settings page.

claims.claim: IncludeProgressFeedback reports files to be labeled, files labeled in the last seven days and total labeled files for enabled policies.
claims.quote: If you use this switch, the command shows the progress of files to be labeled, files labeled in the last 7 days, and total files labeled for enabled auto-labeling policies.
